I'm an independent contributor to the Qiskit open-source ecosystem. My background is in mathematics — number theory, graph theory, and formal proof in Lean 4 — and I've carried that instinct for formal correctness into quantum tooling: circuit libraries and diagnostics built to be verifiably right, not just empirically working.

Recent work includes **Qiberis**, a backend-agnostic circuit library spanning Qiskit Aer, Cirq, and PennyLane, and **qiskit-sqd-dashboard**, a live convergence widget for sample-based quantum diagonalization. Both are documented on the [projects page](index.qmd).

I've also worked through the Qiskit Global Summer School curriculum — GHZ state construction and depth optimization, noise models and dynamic circuits, advanced error mitigation (ZNE, PEC, PNA, SLC, noise learning), and SQD/QAOA applications to molecular simulation and combinatorial optimization.

Outside of Qiskit, I write explainer content on math and quantum topics using Manim, Observable Framework, and Quarto, and I work on original research in graph theory — structures related to modular arithmetic and their component topology.
